review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the SimplicialSet and AlgebraicTopology directories for competing notions. The `SSet.Nonsingular` class is the only definition of this concept; the other files that mention it use it. `Nonsingular.iso` is a named wrapper around `Subcomplex.toOfSimplex` (StdSimplex.lean) and `Subcomplex.isIso_toOfSimplex_iff`. It adds an isomorphism with a `simps!` lemma and does not duplicate them. `N.monoOfLE` is a chosen morphism built from `N.le_iff_exists_mono` and the `PartialOrder X.N` instance (NonDegenerateSimplices.lean). It is a new API with uniqueness, not a competing order or morphism structure. `Nonsingular.of_iso`, `of_mono`, and the nerve, stdSimplex and product instances all use existing constructions. I found no independent duplicate declaration in Mathlib, Batteries or core, so I am abstaining.
